channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
item.description: Replaces dense BF16 KV-cache storage and full-sequence decode attention with NVFP4 packed cache, FP4 query-key scoring over the full history, and sparse FP16 value aggregation over selected 128-token blocks. Costs include Blackwell-generation hardware (GB300-class FP4 tensor cores), calibration of key centering and up to two BF16 pages per sequence and layer, and a fixed per-head block budget that caps attended context. Accuracy losses appear at smaller budgets (64 blocks on some models), gains are demonstrated only on Blackwell hardware unavailable to most constrained setups, and speedups may not transfer to non-Hopper/Blackwell GPUs or API-served models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SpecSearch: Towards Hardware-Aware Efficient Speculative Decoding
item.description: SpecSearch replaces static speculative decoding configurations and manual draft-length tuning with an automated hardware-aware search that jointly optimizes decoding strategy, draft length, and precision using an analytical cost model. It requires infrastructure for multi-GPU calibration or training a specialized predictor, adding engineering complexity beyond standard inference serving. The method can fail when deploying on hardware or workloads outside the calibration distribution, or if the performance predictor mispredicts throughput on unseen architectures. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness
item.description: It replaces repeated per-decision invocation of an LLM reasoner with a small fast System-1 policy guided by a modular harness (procedures, state memory, world models) built and revised asynchronously by the LLM, with utility-driven retrieval. The cost is a two-model architecture: harness storage and retrieval, an extra training/serving path for the System-1 model, continued (though declining) System-2 revision calls, and the engineering complexity of feedback-driven module updates. It can fail when the harness accumulates stale or incorrect modules, when utility retrieval selects misleading context on novel states, or when System-2 revisions degrade rather than improve decision quality. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Surfacing Disagreement Beats Resolving It: A Gated Ablation Study of Provenance-Weighted Memory for Multi-Agent Debate
item.description: This technique replaces standard shared-memory retrieval that silently resolves contradictions by returning a single winning fact. It instead preserves contradictions and passes the ranked conflict set to the debate, at equal operational cost. The main failure risk is implementation-sensitive: conflict sets are built only over retrieved edges, so a retrieval cap can make most planted contradictions unretrievable and drastically reduce the measured benefit; additionally, once contradictions reach the prompt, some mechanisms such as a write trust-gate or provenance routing can reduce accuracy. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SciWorkBench: A Benchmark for Real Scientific Workflows
item.description: SciWorkBench replaces ad hoc or single-step evaluations of scientific agents with a peer-reviewed, workflow-level benchmark spanning biology, chemistry, materials science, and physics, executed under Claude Code and Codex frameworks. It costs the engineering effort of setting up agent execution and grading infrastructure, plus API or compute spend for running frontier models, and it does not itself improve any production system. Adoption risk is low utility for the reader: the benchmark diagnoses weaknesses in frontier scientific agents rather than offering a technique to deploy, and its tasks may not match the reader's domain. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: JET: Just-Enough Exploration Tuning for Efficient Tool-Calling Agents in Repository-Level Question Answering
item.description: Replaces standard SFT on full expert trajectories with trajectories truncated at the point of sufficiency plus a rationale. Costs the pipeline to determine sufficiency and insert rationales; no memory or latency increase. Can fail if truncation removes exploration that would have corrected an early wrong answer, lowering score on ambiguous questions. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
item.description: The method replaces manual, static design of safety harnesses for tool-using agents with automated evolutionary search that optimizes executable harness code against utility and attack-success objectives. It costs significant inference compute for the tree-search evolution loop (using API models or a local evaluator model) plus engineering effort to set up benchmarks, evaluators, and stressor evolution, and it adds a harness layer that affects runtime behavior. It can fail through overfitting to the specific benchmark and attack distribution, degraded protection on harder benchmarks (attack success remains 62.0% on Agent-SafetyBench), regression under adaptive attackers who evolve against the fixed harness, and utility loss if the harness blocks legitimate instructions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The Between-Round Decision in Autonomous Research: An LLM Controller That Reads the Whole Trajectory
item.description: Replaces rule-based, score-based, or search-tree controllers in autonomous research loops with a single LLM call that reads full trajectory history to decide whether to refine the current champion or start a new direction. Costs one additional LLM inference per experimental round plus the context window capacity to hold accumulated evidence, which grows with trajectory length. Can fail when the trajectory history exceeds effective context limits, when the LLM misjudges which past solution to build from, or when the domain lacks clear verified metrics for the controller to ground its decisions. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CrossEnv: Synthesizing Verifiable Cross-Environment Tasks for Long-Horizon Agent Training
item.description: The method replaces hand-curated, single-environment agent training tasks with automatically synthesized cross-environment tasks built on an entity-tool graph, combined with a curriculum that scales from single-environment tool use to multi-service coordination. The cost is the engineering effort required to construct and maintain the entity-tool graph, align cross-environment data for executability and verifiability, and generate sufficient synthetic task volume, which is non-trivial for a small team. Failure modes include data inconsistency across environments breaking task verifiability, synthetic task distribution mismatch with real production workloads reducing transfer, and the graph construction becoming a bottleneck as new services or APIs are added. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Passing Checks Do Not Establish Completion: Evidence Interpretation in Coding Agents
item.description: The technique replaces ad-hoc verification in coding agents with qualified repository checks and controlled evidence consumers to ensure execution facts are preserved and obligations discharged. It costs added workflow complexity for receipts, repairs, and lifetime controls without requiring extra hardware or training. Passing checks may fail to establish completion if facts are misreported or scope is exceeded, limiting diagnostic superiority. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
item.description: SCoRe replaces summary-based continuation by compacting context at stop bursts and marking impossibility judgments as unproven. It costs the compute and latency of extended agent execution up to thousands of turns, plus the complexity of managing context summaries. It can fail by consuming excessive API budget or context window on unproductive tasks without yielding further verified gains. 0 independent implementations, 2134 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
item.description: BORN replaces hand-configured general-purpose quantum chemistry packages with coding agents that synthesize task-specific high-performance programs, selecting algorithmic components from a predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier before execution. It costs an agent-driven synthesis phase plus the infrastructure to extrapolate error from small systems and measure hardware throughputs, and the headline gains are estimated against baselines rather than measured end-to-end. Adoption can fail if small-system error extrapolation mispredicts target-scale accuracy, if runtime prediction misses actual hardware behavior, or if the reader's workloads lie outside the demonstrated Hartree-Fock-style calculations. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop
item.description: The method replaces letting coding agents run until their self-imposed termination by replaying recorded runs, scoring intermediate patches with hidden tests, and applying stopping or earlier-patch-selection rules. It costs evaluation infrastructure for anytime replay with hidden tests and, for the fine-tuning variant, a training pipeline; the stopping rules themselves are cheap heuristics. Adoption can fail because the preregistered quality test does not establish non-inferiority: stopping early may discard patch changes that would have repaired the solution, and savings vary sharply by model and scaffold. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
item.description: The technique replaces unconditional full re-rendering and blocking build-check-render pipelines in code-to-video agent workflows with a training-free execution layer that caches frames by drawing commands and runs checks before rendering at idle priority. It costs additional CPU for speculative rendering that may be discarded when checks fail, plus the complexity of integrating an execution layer behind existing agent commands. It can fail when frame keys miss due to genuinely new content, when recent build history mispredicts check outcomes and wastes render compute, and in domains where the agent's edits rarely produce reusable frames. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway
item.description: SEAM replaces single-screen safety benchmarks by testing cross-screen compositional harm detection in computer-use agents. It costs minimal infrastructure as it relies on server-log scoring and pre-built tasks, though integration into existing CI/CD pipelines requires engineering effort. However, agents may pass the benchmark by relying on user instruction cues without robust reasoning when facts are presented separately. 1 independent implementation, 2135 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory
item.description: It replaces direct VLM solving and visual chain-of-thought (e.g., Canvas-CoT) with an inference-time harness that registers physical scopes, constructs derived views, and invalidates dependent claims on revision, without weight updates. Cost is extra inference calls, generated derived views, and bookkeeping of a scope-aware working memory, increasing latency and orchestration complexity while remaining API-compatible. It can fail when proposed revisions or scope links are themselves wrong, when dependent invalidation is incomplete, and the reported gains may not transfer beyond physics-diagram reasoning. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Values Shape What Self-Improving Coding Agents Build
item.description: The method replaces value-neutral persistent instruction files in self-improving coding agents with short human-written value statements (from Schwartz's higher-order value types) that steer both what the agent builds and how it performs. It costs little in memory, latency, or infrastructure, since it is only an instruction-file change, but it adds a design step that the paper shows cannot be delegated: agent-revised values converge and AI-literature-derived values give no detectable gain. It can fail if the wrong value set is chosen (conservation values degraded performance below baseline) and requires workload-specific validation plus continued human oversight of value design. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue
item.description: Replaces static or purely LLM-driven task allocation with a probabilistic framework that uses dialogue to reduce uncertainty in multi-agent coordination. Costs include maintaining explicit belief states, implementing structured communication protocols, and added decision and coordination overhead. It can fail if belief models are misspecified, dialogue is unreliable or misinterpreted, or the environment is too dynamic for the Bayesian updates to remain accurate. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Inference after coding agents
item.description: The method replaces uncorrected classical inference after agent-driven data analysis with a post-hoc replay procedure: reset the agent on subsamples of the data to estimate the probability it would select the reported analysis when it is statistically favorable, then adjust the test conditional on selection. The cost is substantial additional agent compute (multiple black-box replays per analysis, which scales with API or GPU budget) plus engineering to snapshot and replay the exact agent environment; statistical validity requires that the agent's selection behavior be stable across replays. It can fail if the agent's behavior is non-deterministic, drifts between runs, depends on unreplayable state, or if the subsample design does not approximate the original selection process; nominal coverage is only guaranteed asymptotically and conditional on stable selection. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Identifying and Repairing Energy Smells with Agent Skills
item.description: The technique replaces manual energy profiling and ad-hoc optimization with an agent-guided workflow that detects and repairs energy smells using a taxonomy of 12 patterns and 65 root causes. It requires integrating a static analyzer, verifier, and LLM agent into the development environment, adding complexity and dependency on model behavior. It can fail through false positives, incorrect repairs, or unverified energy claims when measurements are noisy or behavior preservation is not properly validated. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
item.description: This method replaces the manual, human-designed optimization loop with an autonomous process where a frozen LLM constructs its own self-learning algorithm using basic primitives and a compute budget. The cost involves significant expenditure of the allocated compute budget for experimentation and requires access to a sufficiently capable, likely proprietary, LLM, introducing unpredictability in resource consumption. The primary failure mode is the dependency on model capability; less capable models may fail to develop effective strategies, leading to wasted compute resources and a lack of performance improvement. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
item.description: StringQFT replaces ad hoc sourcing of string-theory and QFT reference material with a curated 18-volume textbook collection plus a local lexical retriever, benchmark items, and 19 finite-domain calculation tools for AI-assisted theoretical physics. It costs the effort of hosting or indexing roughly 3,795 pages locally and wiring the retriever and tools into an agent workflow, with no foundation-model training required. It can fail through lexical-retrieval misses on mathematical notation, tool outputs that are correct only within their specified finite domains, and limited transfer to general ML engineering work. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Memory-Efficient Speculative Decoding with Quantized Draft KV Cache
item.description: This method replaces the BF16 key-value cache typically used by the draft model in speculative decoding with a quantized 4-bit cache (K4V4) using per-channel keys and per-token values. The cost is a negligible drop in mean acceptance rate (less than 1.4% relative), while significantly reducing VRAM overhead. Failure can occur if the quantizer layout is not co-designed with the bit-split; naive per-token quantization of keys causes severe acceptance degradation compared to the proposed grouped per-channel approach. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Contrastive Activation-Guided Zeroth-Order Preference Optimisation for Memory-Efficient LLM Alignment
item.description: The method replaces backpropagation-based DPO with zeroth-order optimisation in which perturbations are confined to a low-rank subspace built from the activation discrepancy between chosen and rejected responses, with momentum kept in low-rank coordinates. It eliminates activation-memory cost and cuts peak GPU memory by roughly 59% at sequence length 2048, at the price of the slower convergence and higher gradient-estimation variance typical of zeroth-order methods. Validation covers only a 1.5B model on one preference dataset, so results may not transfer to larger models, longer training runs, or other alignment objectives, and ZO training can require many more forward passes to match first-order quality. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Calibrate Once, Grow the Vocabulary: Candidate-Independent Scores for Conformal Risk Control in Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
item.description: The method replaces per-vocabulary conformal recalibration with scoring each candidate label against a fixed reference bank, making scores invariant to added class names so one calibration retains its risk guarantee as the vocabulary grows. It costs no training and little overhead, but prediction sets can grow by up to roughly one extra label per pixel, and the bounded miss rate for added names holds only if annotated names are a random sample of names in the calibration images, with excess bounded by the gap in mean miss rate otherwise. It can fail when that random-sample assumption is violated, e.g., when harder or adversarially chosen names are added, and it applies only to open-vocabulary segmentation or detection pipelines that use conformal risk control. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Instant Weight-Space Consolidation for Long-Term Memory in LLMs
item.description: It replaces agentic text-extraction memory pipelines and serving-time fine-tuning with a recurrent hypernetwork that compiles session activations into a low-rank adapter in a single forward pass, plus a fixed-size episodic buffer. Cost is a trained hypernetwork and per-session forward passes with fixed memory footprint, but the method requires training or obtaining the consolidation hypernetwork and validating it on the reader's models and memory workloads. It can fail where consolidation loses verbatim detail, where cross-session patterns are sparse, or where distribution shift makes the pre-trained hypernetwork underperform text retrieval. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB: An Open and Efficient Small Language Model for Fast Conversational Agents
item.description: It replaces serving a stock instruction-tuned 4B model (Gemma-4-E4B-it or Qwen3.5-4B) with a further post-trained 4B variant plus a bundled speculative drafter for single-user conversational and tool-use workloads. It costs the extra memory and engineering complexity of loading and maintaining the DFlash drafter alongside the base model, and acceptance-rate tuning for your latency profile. Reported gains are measured at concurrency 1 on RTX/Jetson-class hardware, so speedups can degrade under batched serving, and the 21-benchmark accuracy claim may not transfer to domain-specific tasks without re-evaluation. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Building Fully On-Device GUI Agents with Mobile NPUs
item.description: DroidPrefill replaces conventional autoregressive reasoning and action generation in GUI agents with a prefill-centric architecture optimized for mobile NPUs, combining reduced decoding with context management under fixed compiled budgets. It requires restructuring agent logic for NPU constraints and managing context statically, which increases design complexity. Failures may arise from context truncation, poor generalization to dynamic tasks, or reliance on specific mobile NPU behavior. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Practical Semantic Communication for General-Purpose Networks: Compression of High-Dimensional Embeddings Under Quantization
item.description: Replaces task-agnostic scalar/vector quantization of embeddings with a learned compression matrix optimized under a relaxed Gaussian Information Bottleneck objective with closed-form gradients. Costs: an offline training/optimization step per task and embedding type, plus channel-model assumptions; compute is modest but requires task labels or a target variable. Can fail when the channel model or noise statistics are misestimated, when the downstream task shifts (the compression is task-specific), or on non-text modalities not validated in the paper. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
item.description: This benchmark replaces ad-hoc or synthetic evaluations of coding agents with standardized, application-level CPU optimization tasks derived from scientific workloads. It requires infrastructure to execute programs and verify correctness, introducing overhead in environment setup and compute time. Coordination failures can occur because identical source code varies from 0.29x to 2.12x depending on build settings, and individual optimizations may yield 1.01x or 6.4x depending on interaction with other changes. 2 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Multi-LLM Agentic AI at the Edge: Joint Agent Scheduling and Resource Allocation
item.description: This method replaces ad-hoc agent dispatch with a formal edge-based supervisor-worker architecture that jointly optimizes agent selection and resource allocation (bandwidth, service time, retrieval) via alternating optimization to minimize energy under latency constraints. It requires deploying LLM workers on edge infrastructure with specific hardware constraints and implementing complex optimization solvers (SCA, KKT, Gale-Shapley), which conflicts with the reader's single 24 GB GPU or API-based constraints and limited cloud budget. Failure modes include violation of task latency deadlines under resource contention, suboptimal convergence of the alternating optimization in dynamic edge environments, and brittleness in the two-level retry mechanism when facing heterogeneous worker failures. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Navital Gym: Rule-Graded Agent Environments for Indian Workflows
item.description: This replaces LLM-judged evaluation and generic agent benchmarks with deterministic rule-based grading on synthetic Indian workflow sandboxes. It requires building and maintaining domain-specific rule engines for payments, tax, and multilingual support, which adds engineering cost and limits coverage to predefined workflows. The rules are documented simplifications of Indian practice, not live systems, so agent performance may not transfer to production environments with real regulatory complexity and edge cases. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: LEDGER: Auditable Agent Memory Under Change
item.description: The method replaces full-history replay, raw-transcript retrieval, and opaque memory stores like Mem0 with a structured ledger where explicit rules—not the model—decide currency, source precedence, and deletion, plus an episodic search fallback scrubbed on deletion requests. The cost is a memory-writing pipeline (an LLM pass to propose facts), rule maintenance, and a search component, though inference context shrinks to roughly 1% of full replay. What can fail: the main benchmark is synthetic and self-built, LongMemEval gains are within confidence intervals, and correctness depends on the fact-extraction model and rule coverage of the specific workload. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: GRACE: Parallel Best-of-N Multi-Agent Analysis of Closed-Form Questions over Dataframes with Guardrail Selection and Adaptive Retry
item.description: Replaces single-rollout code generation and scalar-based voting with parallel best-of-N execution and artifact-based guardrail selection that can abstain when all candidates are incorrect. Costs increased API/token usage or GPU memory for concurrent agents and added system complexity for the tournament and retry logic. Can fail when guardrail validation incorrectly rejects valid answers or when the computational overhead of N parallel rollouts exceeds latency constraints. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
item.description: This method replaces generative LLM-based tool use with a deterministic compiler and a small decision model that selects tools and arguments via multiple-choice classification. It costs significantly less memory and compute than running a local LLM and eliminates hallucinated values in tool calls by design. It can fail when the agent must reason over implicit context, handle novel tool combinations not covered by the compiled options, or manage complex multi-step planning that requires generative flexibility. 0 independent implementations, 131 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
item.description: ELITE replaces the evaluate-and-select evolutionary loop, which requires costly repeated execution of candidate agents on downstream tasks, with an Explore-then-Integrate approach that merges complementary code mechanisms based on structural validity checks. The cost is a shift from direct performance-based selection to a complex, multi-step synthesis process that still requires significant LLM inference for proposing, implementing, and inspecting code changes. This can fail if the deterministic validity checks are insufficient to guarantee functional correctness, leading to the integration of subtly broken mechanisms or a failure to resolve logical conflicts between components, resulting in a non-viable descendant agent. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
item.description: Replaces separate specialized models for molecular graphs, biological sequences, and spectra with a single shared multimodal backbone using modality-specific projectors. Requires training a 320B-parameter MoE from scratch, constructing verifiable tool-use environments, and maintaining dedicated encoders, all demanding cluster-scale resources. The approach fails for the reader due to prohibitive training cost and the inability to run such large-scale architectures on constrained local hardware. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SWE-WhatIf: Simulating Real Users of Coding Agents from Recorded Session
item.description: It replaces static replay of recorded user-agent sessions with an LLM-based user simulator that adapts replies to new agent trajectories. It costs LLM inference per simulated turn, plus effort to model user intents and satisfaction criteria from recordings. It can fail when the simulator drifts from real user behavior, when intent models are wrong, or when evaluation conclusions overfit to the 89-session corpus. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Linglong Agent Service: A Runtime for Centralized Agent Reasoning and Distributed Execution
item.description: Replaces ad-hoc agent-tool integration by treating execution site as a configurable dimension, keeping reasoning and state on a parent service while routing file, shell, terminal, and MCP operations to remote child environments via HTTP or WebSocket tunnels. Costs include additional infrastructure complexity, latency from remote tool calls, and unimplemented features like runtime patch activation and failed-call recovery. Can fail due to unproven performance advantages, repair accuracy, or production recovery capabilities, and the core path's lack of third-party dependencies may limit functionality. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
item.description: RepoFactory replaces linear repository-to-environment pipelines that stop at validation with an Environment Evolution Loop that uses proxy feedback to jointly optimize validity, structural coupling, and implementation scope across 17 software domains. Adoption requires constructing and maintaining a scalable evolution loop and proxy evaluation infrastructure, with costs in pipeline complexity, compute for generating and validating 10k+ environments, and potential engineering effort to adapt to proprietary codebases; the paper does not quantify inference latency or memory overhead. Proxy signals can misalign with actual training value, evolved environments may overfit to specific repository distributions or benchmarks, and verifiable feedback mechanisms can fail on real-world production code that deviates from training domains. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?
item.description: Replaces passive waiting for user edit requests with proactive LLM-generated suggestions filtered by a trained decision model. Costs include training and maintaining a separate gating model, plus inference overhead for the recommendation generator. Can fail on inherently unpredictable real-world requests that the gating mechanism does not perfectly filter, leading to either missed suggestions or false positives. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Feature Representation Changes Local Explanations: A Controlled Comparison of SHAP and LIME under Numerical Discretization
item.description: This is a diagnostic finding, not a deployable method: it replaces nothing, but shows that treating SHAP/LIME attributions as statements about the underlying continuous quantity must give way to treating them as statements about the quantized effective input. Adoption costs a sensitivity audit—re-running explanations across candidate discretizations and comparing against a seed-noise floor—which adds compute and pipeline complexity for a constrained team. It can fail because the frozen-model design cannot separate representation effects from effective-input effects, and results derive from one dataset (UCI Adult), one model class (random forest), and one feature (age), so findings may not transfer. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A COMPASS to the Galaxy: Joint nucleosynthetic yield set comparison and parameter inference in Galactic chemical evolution
item.description: The method replaces repeated likelihood-based inference or likelihood-free approximations for each dataset with an amortized conditional score-based diffusion model that jointly infers parameters and ranks competing model prescriptions. It costs the upfront generation of forward simulations plus training of a transformer-based diffusion model, and it adds architectural and validation complexity compared with standard posterior-only SBI. It can fail if the training simulations are misspecified, if observational data shift away from the simulated distribution, or if the learned likelihood and model ranking are sensitive to those mismatches. 0 independent implementations, 17 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Scientific Coding with Large Language Models: Evidence from Finite Element Analysis
item.description: This replaces single-pass LLM code generation and single-agent self-verification with an agentic harness that separates code production from independent test generation and execution-based revision. It costs repeated model calls and code executions per task, roughly three or more attempts plus tester-agent overhead, which increases API spend and latency relative to one-shot prompting. It can still fail because generated tests may share errors with the implementation (28.5% of analyzed failures) or provide inadequate coverage (73.1%), so independent verification does not eliminate correlated mistakes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MiSTiQ: MicroScaling Trellis Quantization for Extreme KV Cache Compression
item.description: MiSTiQ replaces codebook-based vector quantizers in the KV cache with trellis-coded storage using beam search, producing reconstructions directly in MX formats such as NVFP4 so attention can run in low precision. The cost is encoding complexity (beam search per block), implementation effort for MX-Hash functions, and dependence on hardware or kernels that support MX formats for compute-side gains. It can fail if production kernels lack NVFP4 or MX support, if the compression gains do not survive on the reader's actual workload distribution, or if integration with an existing serving stack (e.g., vLLM) requires custom kernel work the team cannot maintain. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SURMA: Efficient Fine-Grained Communication Offload for SuperPOD
item.description: SURMA replaces SM-driven remote memory access with a dedicated on-die RDMA engine featuring credit-based shared send queues, fused write-with-atomic semantics, and Network Per Path Ordering to eliminate head-of-line blocking and ordering stalls. The cost is silicon area (under 0.5% of GPU die) and the complexity of custom RTL implementation and hardware fabrication. The approach fails entirely without access to SuperPOD-class infrastructure with NVLink and the ability to modify or procure custom accelerator hardware. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Agent-Native by Design: A Programming Language for Agentic Applications
item.description: Jac replaces hand-written glue code over SDKs/agent frameworks by embedding typed LLM calls, tool use, workflow state, and model-guided routing into a Python-superset language with shared execution semantics. The cost is adopting a new language/runtime and its ecosystem constraints, with compiler-visible control flow offered as the main mechanism for optimization claims. It can fail if the promised analyses, speculative execution, or service partitioning do not preserve behavior under real workloads, or if the smaller ecosystem and tooling maturity increase delivery risk. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Turing Agent: Agentic Formal Verification for Mathematical Research
item.description: Replaces direct LLM generation and general-purpose coding harnesses with a multi-agent pipeline that decomposes, formalizes, and machine-checks research-level proofs. Costs include orchestrating many agents, iterative verification loops, and semantic review, implying high token and infrastructure demands that exceed a single 24 GB GPU. Failures include incorrect decomposition, unfaithful formalization, and undetected semantic errors. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Latent Bridge: Asking for Help Without Words
item.description: The method replaces text-based handoff from a large model, where the sender first decodes an intermediate response, with prefill-only hidden-state transfer through a trainable bridge that injects extra attention keys and values into the receiver. It costs sender prefill compute during inference, additional bridge training and integration complexity, and some receiver-side attention overhead while preserving the receiver KV cache; large-model autoregressive decoding is removed, but inference is not free. It can fail if the sender and receiver representations do not align well, if periodic review adds latency without enough quality benefit, or if cross-family transfer does not hold for the reader's exact models and tasks. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Syllable- and Word-Level Evaluation of Tibetan OCR
item.description: It replaces sole reliance on character error rate with syllable error rate and segmented word error rate for Tibetan OCR evaluation. It adds evaluation complexity and requires a segmenter only for SWER, while SER avoids that dependency and needs no model or infrastructure change. CER can fail because it may reverse the ranking of a system pair and does not establish which systems preserve named entities at 0.6. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Programmable Semantic Interventions: Learning Causal Carriers from Behavioral Programs
item.description: PSI replaces the need for curated counterfactual datasets and ground-truth labels in mechanistic interpretability by allowing investigators to define causal interventions via semantic programs that read expected answers directly from the frozen model. It requires training a low-rank activation subspace on a 24 GB GPU, which is feasible but adds complexity to the interpretability pipeline and may require careful tuning to match the model's behavior. Failure modes include misalignment if the model's internal representations do not cleanly factor into the declared semantic variables, leading to unreliable interventions or poor steering performance in production. 0 independent implementations, 7 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TEMPO: Regime-Aware Operator Learning with Locally Adapted POD Bases
item.description: TEMPO replaces a single global POD basis in PDE operator learning with a mixture of locally adapted bases discovered via EM, plus a gating network that routes inputs to per-regime branch networks. The cost is a two-phase training pipeline, added model complexity from gating and per-regime branches, and sensitivity to the EM regime discovery and routing quality. It can fail when the latent regimes are ill-separated, when the gating network misroutes inputs at inference, or when the parameter regimes in deployment data drift from those recovered offline. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Representational Change Under Self-Consuming Training: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis
item.description: This research analyzes the internal representations of language models that are recursively trained on their own synthetic outputs, a scenario known as self-consuming training. It does not propose a new method to replace an existing one, but rather uses sparse autoencoders (SAEs) as a diagnostic tool to study this phenomenon. The work's cost is the significant research effort required to train multiple generations of models and probes. A key finding is that SAEs trained on an original model degrade in performance when applied to later generations, indicating representational drift; this failure means that reconstruction fidelity alone is an insufficient measure of an SAE's interpretive utility after model updates. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
item.description: The method replaces single-pass chain-of-thought detection and rigid multi-agent workflows with a coordinating investigator agent plus a library of forensic inspector sub-agents trained via dual-timescale policy optimization. It costs the curated ForenCue-30K annotation corpus, two-level reinforcement learning with annotated artifact intervals, and multi-model orchestration, none of which is reproducible on a 24 GB GPU or a limited API budget. It can fail when deployed against generators outside its benchmark coverage, when the investigator-inspector feedback loop amplifies annotation biases, and when forensic cues disappear under recompression or adversarial post-processing. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Variational Monte Carlo for Quantum Excited States via Nested Low-Rank Approximation
item.description: It replaces the need to compute K^2 Laplacians per step in NES-VMC or to tune overlap-penalty weights in penalty-based excited-state VMC by reparameterizing the rank-K variational objective with a low-rank approximation. The cost is implementing a specialized VMC-compatible stochastic gradient estimator with MCMC sampling from per-state Born densities plus a sequential nesting scheme, with the paper not providing a quantified speedup or production latency figure. What can fail is the MCMC sampling and optimization becoming unstable or inaccurate for larger systems, and the method may not transfer to engineering workloads because it is specific to solving the electronic Schrödinger equation. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: A Scalable Multi Task Learning Framework for Modeling Demographic Disagreements in Annotation Tasks
item.description: The method replaces single-task annotation models that aggregate labels uniformly across annotator groups. It incurs computational cost to train multiple group-conditional models and requires demographic membership data. Performance may degrade if group labels are sparse, missing, or if the group structure does not align with actual disagreement patterns. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Is This Code Mine? Student Ownership When AI Agents Write the Spec and the Code
item.description: Replaces output-based code review and grading with enforced process verification that validates what engineers specify, review, and can explain rather than what AI agents ship. Costs the implementation of repository mining, commit auditing, and process enforcement tools, plus the operational overhead of validating human comprehension separately from generated artifacts. Can fail if teams game the process by backdating specifications or generating unused code to meet volume targets, or if ownership claims remain unverifiable against actual commit history. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Beyond Leaderboard Ranks: Selecting Software Engineering Agents Under Budget Constraints
item.description: It replaces exhaustive full-benchmark evaluation and leaderboard-rank-based agent selection with an uncertainty-aware adaptive allocation strategy (successive halving) that accounts for statistical indistinguishability and validated execution costs. It costs additional evaluation infrastructure and complexity, and its advantage narrows when task costs are unknown before execution or when exact-best selection is required. Reported agent costs can differ from standardized token-based estimates by up to 11.7x, and selective task evaluation can bias full-benchmark cost estimates, so cost validation can fail if these factors are ignored. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Safe Resemblance, Silent Propagation: Limits of Text-Similarity Guardrails for AI Agent Safety
item.description: The paper argues that text-similarity guardrails like DonkeyRail fail to distinguish between malicious instruction propagation and legitimate quotation in AI agent communications. The method replaces behavioral analysis with surface-level text matching, requiring continuous calibration and producing high false positive rates that vary across different templates and use cases. The approach fails when identical visible transcripts require different safety decisions based on governing policies, which observation-only classifiers cannot resolve. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Procedure without Judgment: What Small Language Models Learn under an Exact Verifier
item.description: The method replaces proxy-based explanation scoring and frontier-model distillation with exact algorithmic verification of minimal sufficient reasons for policy decisions. It requires an enumerable context space and executable policy to compute ground truth, plus 2000 verified traces for fine-tuning a 4B model, fitting within a 24GB GPU budget. Learned schedules overfit to the training policy and fail to transfer: answers remain sufficient but stop being minimal on unseen policies, and reinforcement learning from the exact reward inverts strategy without improving generalization. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
item.description: CertiSum replaces non-deterministic MXFP4 training with a certification mechanism that ensures bitwise-identical results across platforms by verifying exactness or recomputing outputs. It costs an 11.8-60.5% increase in training-step latency relative to standard MXFP4 and requires specific hardware support for MXFP4. Failure can occur if certification rates are low, forcing expensive exact recomputation that negates performance benefits. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
item.description: The Lattice replaces the standard Transformer residual stream (and the internal states of SSM/linear-attention hybrids) by adding persistent per-layer horizontal latent streams that directly condition attention, KV-cache writes, MLP computation, and decoding. It requires training from scratch with increased architectural complexity and a larger state footprint than parameter-matched baselines, though exact inference latency and memory costs are not quantified in the abstract. Adoption can fail because benefits are demonstrated only at the 406M scale on 20B tokens, and the recurrent latents may introduce unforeseen training instabilities or deployment overheads that negate perplexity gains at production scale. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Decomposing Earth Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders
item.description: The technique replaces raw opaque Earth observation embeddings with sparse, approximately monosemantic features learned by a sparse autoencoder over an overcomplete dictionary. It costs additional compute and engineering effort to train and evaluate SAEs, requires a tailored protocol for spatial data, and does not yet provide reliable downstream application performance. What can fail is that many proposed benefits, such as interpretability and fine spatial-scale variance, also arise from sparsity alone with a random decoder, while the two tested applications remain insufficiently reliable for practical use. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
item.description: This replaces the default conservative practice of running on-policy distillation rollouts in BF16 with synchronous generation, substituting model-specific FP8 rollout recipes plus an admission check that screens rollout configurations against a calibrated mismatch budget before training. The cost is a one-time per-model calibration of sensitive layers and mismatch budget, added system complexity from asynchronous rollouts, and some residual quality loss if the budget is exceeded. It can fail when a model's sensitivity pattern differs from the calibrated pairs, when injected mismatch shifts generated prefixes beyond what per-token corrections fix, or when the admission check is miscalibrated and an unstable configuration is admitted. 0 independent implementations, 26 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Semantically Aligned KV Cache Compression for Efficient Agentic Autoregressive Video Generation
item.description: It replaces generic, per-generator KV-cache eviction in agentic autoregressive video generation with training-free top-k retention scored by planner-extracted semantic constraints via text cross-attention. It costs group-wise attention scoring and selection overhead per candidate while leaving keys, values, and positions unchanged, with reported quality essentially at Full KV level. It can fail when text cross-attention misidentifies constraint-relevant positions, when workloads lack explicit planner constraints, or when results on the four evaluated backbones do not transfer to the reader's stack. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TID System for Speech-COSER Challenge 2026: ASR Track
item.description: The method replaces full fine-tuning of an ASR model with a two-stage LoRA curriculum in which CTC pseudo-forced alignment scores filter or order training samples by audio-text match quality, followed by post-hoc magnitude pruning of the LoRA matrices. It costs little in memory since only low-rank adapters are trained, but adds pipeline complexity: alignment scoring, curriculum staging, pruning, and a seven-system ROVER ensemble for the best result. It can fail if alignment scores mislabel usable training data as mismatched, if pruning removes adapter capacity needed for the target domain, or if the ensemble inference cost is unacceptable in production. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ConvLUT: Rethinking Convolutional Architectures for Ultra-Low-Latency LUT-Based Inference
item.description: ConvLUT replaces conventional convolutional inference (GPU/CPU kernels) with fully unrolled lookup-table networks mapped directly onto FPGA logic, using LUT-tree convolution, channel-partitioned LUT pooling, and hardware-aware iterative pruning. The cost is a specialized FPGA design and synthesis pipeline, tight fan-in constraints that limit model capacity, and accuracy that remains only competitive rather than superior on small-scale benchmarks. Adoption can fail because the workflow requires FPGA hardware and HDL tooling, the method is validated only on tiny vision/audio tasks, and accuracy may degrade on realistic datasets outside CIFAR-10, Visual Wake Words, and Keyword Spotting. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: PRISM: Causal Counterfactual Minimization of Agent Tool Privileges via Information Bottleneck Role Induction
item.description: Replaces coarse, manually assigned or full-permission tool grants over MCP with automatically induced least-privilege roles derived from sandboxed counterfactual interventions and information-bottleneck compression. Costs include an offline phase of sandboxed trajectory collection, intervention experiments, and bilevel optimization with a generative flow network, plus ongoing role re-derivation when tools or tasks change; the inference overhead at runtime is small, but the pipeline adds significant engineering complexity. It can fail when sandbox interventions do not cover real task variability, causing necessary tools to be pruned and degrading task success, or when the rate-distortion knee selects too few roles and forces over-broad grants within a role. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: WETW: Learning Pair-Specific Weighted Euclidean Distances for Efficient DTW Search
item.description: WETW-FV replaces exact quadratic-cost DTW computation over full collections (and weak lower-bound pruning) with a learned filter-and-verify pipeline: a trained encoder (WESEE) embeds series, a small symmetric network predicts pair-specific per-dimension weights for a weighted Euclidean shortlist, and exact DTW verifies only shortlisted candidates. The cost is an offline training stage requiring DTW distance supervision plus ranking regularization (regression alone misorders neighbors, recall@1 of 0.79 versus 0.95), added pipeline complexity, and approximate recall rather than exact search guarantees. It can fail on data distributions that drift from the training set, on workloads where embedding training data is scarce, and where the 0.91-0.93 recall@10 loss is unacceptable for the application. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ERGo: Energy-Efficient Hybrid Graph Neural Network Training on Processing-In-Memory Architectures
item.description: The method replaces full-parameter GNN training on processing-in-memory hardware with a schedule that switches mid-training to a low-rank parameter-efficient phase, reducing off-chip memory access and NVM write operations. It requires PIM or heterogeneous NVM-SRAM hardware and introduces a training schedule with low-rank weight approximations, adding implementation complexity. It can fail if the accuracy loss is not negligible on a given task, if low-rank capacity is insufficient late in training, or if the gains do not transfer to the GPU and API infrastructure the reader actually operates. 3 independent implementations, 129 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: User-Schedulable Approximations for Quantized Tensor Programs
item.description: The method replaces hand-written quantized matmul kernels in GGML/llama.cpp with Halide programs where encoders and decoders are ordinary schedulable stages fused into register tiles via the approximate_by directive, generating hundreds of kernels from one algorithm and schedule library. Adoption costs building on a research fork of Halide, maintaining codec compositions and property-test contracts (e.g. round-trip laws), and accepting per-format performance that only matches handwritten kernels in most (not all) cases. It can fail if the compiler backend does not support your target (x86 AMX port required 793 extra lines), if numerical contracts expose bugs in existing formats (as it did for GGML's q8_1 block sums), or if your production inference stack depends on llama.cpp mainline, which does not use this system. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Pattern-Based Matrix Analysis Under Permutations
item.description: The method replaces manual or heuristic matrix reordering with a formal pattern-distance framework that discovers latent geometric structures in matrices through optimal row and column permutations. It costs computational overhead from solving NP-hard Linear Assignment subproblems iteratively and requires careful pattern specification, with no demonstrated application to inference acceleration, memory reduction, or model quality improvement in resource-constrained settings. It can fail when the assumed pattern does not match the true underlying structure, when the alternating optimization converges to local minima, or when the density-matched random-mask control shows the structure is not meaningfully present. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Antidistillation is Cheap: Lightweight Distillation-Resistance via Stylistic Corruption
item.description: The method replaces surrogate-model next-token sampling defenses with lightweight activation-level style-steering vectors injected only on suspected malicious queries. It costs a small inference-time intervention and activation-space engineering rather than a separate surrogate model, with negligible claimed latency overhead. It can fail if malicious queries are misclassified, if style steering degrades semantic utility or fluency in practice, or if the defense proves sensitive to model and workload specifics. 2 independent implementations, 2256 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
item.description: Replaces per-query calls to a hosted frontier LLM agent with a single-pass 7B text-to-SQL model that handles confident queries locally and escalates only uncertain ones. Costs a 9 GB GPU footprint for the 8-bit quantized model plus the engineering complexity of deploying the bounded-grammar candidate-plan pipeline and trained validator. Can fail on the roughly 32% of queries where the local model's 68% standalone accuracy is wrong but not flagged as uncertain, and on schemas or dialects where the bounded grammar or validator transfers poorly. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CHARMING: Parallel Edge AI Acceleration Across Tensor Processing and In-Memory Computation
item.description: Replaces AIE-only edge inference by partitioning attention heads between the AIE array and an in-DRAM compute unit, with accuracy- and quantization-aware head selection and integrated quantization in the projection stage. Costs include dependence on specific AMD Versal/Alveo platforms, in-memory compute hardware, custom partitioning logic, and potential accuracy loss from head selection and int4 compute. It can fail if the target workload does not fit the assumed head-level partitioning, if int4 degradation exceeds the reported tolerance, or if deployment lacks access to the validated hardware stack. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
item.description: CarryOn replaces summarization, pruning, and full-history retention for long-horizon agents with a compact execution state plus fine-grained, source-linked evidence selected by a learned selector and adaptive retention policy, avoiding extra LLM calls for context management. The cost is training and maintaining the selector model, added system complexity, and reliance on the paper's own evaluation metrics, though inference-time overhead is claimed to be low. It can fail if the learned selector misidentifies which evidence to keep on out-of-distribution tasks, omitting exact details needed for later actions, and the gains are validated only on three benchmarks with specific actor models. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Disentangling Forgetting from Utility: Lightweight LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Null-Space Projection
item.description: UUE replaces fine-tuning-based unlearning by projecting parameter updates into the orthogonal left null space of retained representations, using lightweight pluggable adapters (including a low-rank variant) on a frozen backbone. Costs include adapter training/inference complexity and potential compute for closed-form solutions, though designed to be lightweight. Failure modes include imperfect disentanglement leading to residual knowledge retention or unanticipated utility degradation if the null-space assumption does not hold for all retained knowledge. 3 independent implementations, 2260 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents
item.description: The method replaces ad hoc reactive guardrails or post-hoc rejection with a pre-execution formal verification step against explicit specifications, followed by runtime enforcement that uses the verified plan to guide recovery when actions are blocked. It costs additional planning and verification latency, requires formalizable domain specifications, and adds integration complexity for the plan checker and monitor. It can fail if policies are incomplete or mis-specified, the verifier or environment model is unsound, or the agent cannot find a compliant recovery path. 2 independent implementations, 2135 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Adversarially Attacking Symbolic Vocabulary Vulnerabilities In LLM Planners
item.description: The method replaces manual red-teaming of LLM planning systems with an automated LLM-based attack (Symbolic Swapper) that renames actions, predicates, and objects in PDDL-style domains to strip commonsense cues. Cost is modest: an LLM-driven generation pipeline plus a planner evaluation harness, fitting a single GPU or API-only setup, but it adds an evaluation stage that must be maintained per domain. It can fail to transfer, since obfuscations tuned to break specific models may overstate fragility relative to real deployment distributions, and results on synthetic planning benchmarks may not predict failures of tool-calling agents in production. 3 independent implementations, 2260 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration
item.description: MineralExp replaces unstructured human judgment of open-ended experimental designs with a 19-type taxonomy that converts experimental design into deterministic multi-label classification, supplemented by an LLM-as-a-Judge metric. Adoption costs are low (277 expert-verified cases, API-based scoring) but building an equivalent benchmark in a new domain requires expert annotation and taxonomy design effort. It can fail through taxonomy abstraction that loses domain-critical procedural detail, LLM-judge bias, and because its key finding—that agents over-propose experiments with high recall and low precision—may not transfer to other domains or agent configurations. 2 independent implementations, 5 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
item.description: OutfitterBench replaces generic short-horizon agent evaluations with a 200-day resource-allocation simulation (46-product catalog, ~1,100 reservations, fixed capital ceiling) that tests whether agents keep their own commitments feasible while reassessing allocation value. Adoption costs integration effort against its public codebase and the API inference budget to run 200-day episodes per model, and it provides no production-ready policy, only a diagnostic. It can fail to transfer if the reader's workload lacks comparable commitment structure, and results may overfit to this rental-domain simulation rather than predict behavior in the reader's actual environment. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Can You Trust Your Finance Agent? Drift, Diagnosis and Auditable Intervention on One Shipped Financial Research Agent
item.description: Replaces ad-hoc prompt tuning and leaderboard-score trust with repeated-run stability measurement, trace-based fault attribution by owning layer, and a gated optimization loop that keeps changes only if they beat a pre-registered threshold. Costs include running multiple evaluation passes to quantify variance, maintaining a frozen failure taxonomy, and blind human or multi-model trace review for diagnosis validation. Can fail if run-to-run variance is underestimated on small question sets, leading to false confidence in gains that fall within noise, as the paper itself demonstrates with its accuracy objective. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
item.description: It replaces ad hoc live-site or text-only web-agent evaluation with 300 reproducible tasks across 20 self-hosted applications spanning text, vision, audio, and video. The cost is infrastructure and operational effort to self-host the applications and run isolated parallel evaluations, plus dependence on API access for the strongest agents; it measures agent quality rather than improving it. It can fail to transfer if the reader's production tasks differ from the benchmark's application categories, if self-hosting drifts from the released configurations, or if API model updates change agent behavior between evaluations. 5 independent implementations, 2261 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
item.description: The paper replaces text-only Chinese grammatical error correction with G-CGEC, an image-to-grounded-edit task that requires corrections and their visual positions on handwritten essay images. It costs added pipeline or multi-agent orchestration, OCR and character-grounding components, more latency, and dependence on proprietary or open VLM quality rather than a single deployable model. It can fail because top proprietary models perform poorly in single pass, while linguistic error discovery and character-level grounding remain the primary bottlenecks. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Agent-as-a-Judge
item.description: This approach replaces static LLM-as-a-Judge systems that rely solely on fixed execution logs by introducing active evaluators that autonomously seek external evidence and verify environmental states. It significantly increases operational costs through multi-step agentic inference, tool-use API fees, and orchestration complexity compared to passive, single-pass evaluation methods. The system can fail due to unreliable tool calls, compounding reasoning errors, or when the judge's own agentic capabilities are insufficient to retrieve or interpret the necessary evidence. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
item.description: The method replaces single-pass programmatic 3D reconstruction and direct image-to-video diffusion with a closed-loop framework in which a vision-language coding agent iteratively verifies physical equilibrium and compiles a unified rigid/articulated/cloth/FEM solver whose rollouts condition pretrained video diffusion. It costs substantial engineering complexity, requires a full multiphysics simulation stack and a vision-language agent loop, and adds per-scene iterative verification latency well beyond a single forward pass. It can fail on scenes where monocular depth and support ambiguity remain unresolved after verification, where constitutive parameter estimates are wrong, or where the 81% recovery rate does not transfer to in-the-wild photographs outside the benchmark. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Folding Language Models into Themselves
item.description: This replaces training a compact student from scratch by folding every group of N adjacent teacher layers into a single shared block executed N times, with per-step low-rank corrections and per-token gating initialized from the original layer weights. It costs the compute and data pipeline for distillation on 22B tokens with a curated multi-domain recipe, and adds inference complexity from iterative block execution and gating. It can fail when the low-rank corrections and gates cannot recover layer-specific behaviors for out-of-distribution tasks, or when the 22B-token data mix does not match the target deployment distribution, leaving capabilities unrecovered despite the shared block. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
item.description: iWSP replaces gradient-based training of opaque predictors with an LLM agent that iteratively hand-crafts model weights and features in code to produce human-interpretable computations. It costs iterative LLM-agent reasoning and trial-and-error instead of backpropagation, and may require careful prompt/evaluation design plus compute for repeated LLM calls rather than standard training infrastructure. It can fail if the agent's prior knowledge does not transfer to the domain, if the search over interpretable computations is inefficient or unstable, or if the resulting hand-crafted models underperform less-interpretable baselines in production settings. 0 independent implementations, 67 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
item.description: Replaces static, contamination-prone financial benchmarks with a continuously refreshable Japanese benchmark built by a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline that converts heterogeneous certification exams. Costs are per-edition human verification effort, maintenance of exam-specific conversion code, and API spend if the reader evaluates proprietary models; it is an evaluation asset, not a capability improvement. It can fail through conversion errors that slip past review, edition-to-edition drift that breaks comparability, and limited transfer if the reader's production tasks are not Japanese financial QA. 2 independent implementations, 134 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Large Language Model-Empowered Intelligent Agent for Adaptive Fast-Charging Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries
item.description: Replaces conventional charging protocols, model-based optimization, and task-specific data-driven controllers with an LLM agent fine-tuned (SFT plus GRPO) on a large PyBaMM simulation corpus to emit closed-loop charging actions. Costs include generating a large multi-chemistry simulation corpus, two-stage training, and per-step LLM inference, none of which are quantified; the cycling-life gain is reported only as a comparison without a numeric factor. It can fail on real hardware because all validation is simulation-only, sim-to-real mismatch and per-cell variation can invalidate the learned policy, and LLM inference latency and nondeterminism are problematic for a safety-critical control loop. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
item.description: The method replaces aggregate-alignment prompting with user-specific value profiles measured via standardized psychometric instruments (SVS, PVQ-21, MFQ) used to benchmark LLM-controlled robots against desired robot value profiles. The direct cost is low (questionnaire administration plus standard API benchmarking on existing models, no training), but operationalizing it adds evaluation tooling, per-user profile storage, and a personalization layer whose implementation the paper does not specify. The central failure mode, shown by the paper itself, is that prompting shifts LLM behavior only weakly toward the target profile, so the profiling yields a measurement without a demonstrated mechanism to enforce it, and the N=22 sample limits generalizability of the desired-profile findings. 2 independent implementations, 2135 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Neural Classifiers as Error-Correcting Codes
item.description: The framework does not replace a deployed method; it reinterprets cross-entropy classification as maximum-likelihood decoding over learned codebooks and suggests derived criteria for quantization, distillation, and regularization. Adoption cost is analytical rather than computational, but the abstract reports no experiments, benchmarks, or validated implementations of the proposed criteria. The derived quantization and distillation rules can fail if the theoretical correspondence does not translate into measurable gains on real workloads, and there is no evidence yet that it does. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review
item.description: PrivacyPR replaces ad-hoc or synthetic evaluation of privacy-aware code review with 4,131 real merged GitHub PRs linking actual privacy defects to accepted fixes, including a verified 250+250 split and a 100+100 evaluation subset with a harness that reverts fixes to reintroduce defects. Adoption costs evaluation compute against a hosted or local coding agent plus LLM-judge calls, fitting a single 24 GB GPU or third-party API budget, but requires building prompting and parsing around the provided harness. It can fail through LLM-generated labels with only 72% annotator endorsement, reverting-based defect reintroduction that may not compile or reproduce the original flaw, and high false-positive rates (11-15%) that make raw detector output noisy in production review pipelines. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
item.description: It replaces large-scale cross-database pretraining for relational prediction with a mixture-of-relational-experts graph transformer plus an LLM agent that generates label-blind derived columns from schema statistics. It costs implementing a specialized architecture, training it on available relational corpora, and LLM API calls for column engineering, all with limited tooling outside the RelBench ecosystem. It can fail because gains are demonstrated only on RelBench-style benchmarks, the agent may produce invalid or harmful derived columns on atypical schemas, and production deployment requires bespoke data pipelines rather than off-the-shelf models. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
item.description: It replaces training a dedicated task-specific policy for each robot task family with a closed-loop system in which a frontier foundation model observes, reasons, invokes skills/tools, and verifies outcomes. The cost is a heavy embodied harness, dependence on frontier-model APIs, and substantial evaluation and safety engineering rather than a deployable algorithm. It can fail under real-time constraints, mechanical limits, irreversible errors, and unpredictable environments, and the position paper offers no validated reliability guarantees. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
item.description: The method replaces per-game scripted or bespoke RL agents with a single end-to-end vision-language-action model trained on tens of thousands of hours of keyboard-and-mouse trajectories, plus continued pre-training, sparse-thinking instruction tuning, and multi-turn reinforcement learning. Its cost is exactly what the reader lacks: massive interaction data collection, foundation-model-scale training, and a dedicated cloud-edge serving engine for real-time concurrent inference. For the reader's setting, failure is structural rather than incidental: the approach cannot be reproduced or fine-tuned meaningfully without cluster-scale compute and proprietary-scale trajectory data. 4 independent implementations, 307 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: HerAgent: A Block-Level Checkpointing Harness for Coding-Agent Environment Setup
item.description: HerAgent replaces single-command or whole-script progress control with a unified semantic block abstraction for execution, validation, checkpointing, and rollback. It requires implementing a checkpointing harness with block-level state capture, introducing moderate engineering complexity but no additional hardware requirements. Failure can occur if block boundaries are misaligned with actual dependencies or if state capture mechanisms introduce significant overhead. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
item.description: The method replaces single-view, native-representation verifier accuracy measurement with a matched-view reliability test that checks whether the same verifier's judgments survive abstraction, delegation, and history compaction, plus the practice of attaching execution provenance to abstracted views. Cost is modest engineering overhead: constructing or logging provenance-bearing views of each execution and re-running the verifier per view, which adds verifier API or inference calls roughly proportional to the number of views tested. What can fail is that provenance recovery degrades when provenance is lossy or unavailable, low transport failure can mask over-abstention by evidence-grounded protocols rather than true correctness, and results on four benchmarks may not transfer to domain-specific agent traces. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
item.description: ARCHER replaces free-form chain-of-thought imitation with supervised typed action traces (reasoning steps, calculator calls, runtime observations, verification actions) followed by asymmetric hierarchical reinforcement learning with gated trajectory rewards. The cost is a two-stage training pipeline: rationale-to-trace compilation, a deterministic calculator runtime, and multi-component RL reward infrastructure, plus the engineering burden of maintaining the execution environment. It can fail when compiled traces are noisy or unrepresentative of the target tasks, when the gated rewards are miscalibrated, or when deployed without the same runtime assumptions used during training, and the absolute AIME accuracies of sub-10B models may remain too low for production reliance. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
item.description: The technique replaces manual, case-by-case design of fault-tolerant Clifford circuits for quantum error-correcting codes with LLM-guided evolutionary program synthesis verified by exhaustive fault checking. It costs LLM inference for program evolution, verifier computation, and curated task specification, with no reported inference or memory efficiency gains. It can fail if verifier coverage is incomplete or if synthesized circuits do not generalize beyond the curated tasks, and it is irrelevant to production AI/ML inference or training on constrained GPU/API infrastructure. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.
